claim: Globally, 47.9% of people have serum 25(OH)D below 50 nmol/L (insufficient) and 15.7% have levels below 30 nmol/L (severely deficient), based on 308 studies with 7.9 million participants from 81 countries (2000-2022).
stance_target: Vitamin D deficiency/insufficiency is a global pandemic affecting nearly half the world population
quoted_support: globally, 15·7% (95% CrI 13·7–17·8), 47·9% (95% CrI 44·9–50·9), and 76·6% (95% CrI 74·0–79·1) of participants had serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels less than 30, 50, and 75 nmol/l, respectively

claim: Lower-middle-income countries (a category that includes India) have higher vitamin D deficiency prevalence than higher-income countries, per global pooled analysis.
stance_target: India's lower-middle-income status correlates with elevated vitamin D deficiency burden
scope_conditions: Global; stratified by World Bank income group
quoted_support: the Eastern Mediterranean region and Lower-middle-income countries had a higher prevalence

claim: Vitamin D deficiency prevalence in winter-spring is 1.7 times higher than in summer-autumn globally, indicating seasonal variation relevant to supplementation need.
stance_target: Seasonal variation justifies year-round supplementation in regions with monsoon or winter seasons
quoted_support: the prevalence in winter-spring was 1·7 (95% CrI 1·4–2·0) times that in summer-autumn
